Comment:
Additionally, what is the frequency of occurrence, and what is the likelihood that the combination of high tides and storm water runoff will result in flooding of the Alviso area.
Response:
The Alviso area is relatively flat and has a very poorly developed drainage system. Local ponding of rainwater is common within the area even following light rainfall. The through-flowing Guadalupe River and Coyote Creek do not provide natural drainage to the area since they are diked to prevent over-bank flooding of adjacent lands. As a consequence, run-off within the area is prevented from entering either Guadalupe River or Coyote Creek.
The Alviso area has experienced widespread and severe flooding from creek or river overflows a number of times in the past, and unless further flood control improvements are made, a reoccurrence of this event can be anticipated in the future. Flooding of the area occurred in 1955, 1958, 1963 and 1968, none of which approximated the "one-hundred year" flood level. Protection from the "one-hundred year" flood would require extensive flood control improvements along Coyote Creek and the Guadalupe River north of Highway 237 (Alviso-Milpitas Road) and on the Guadalupe River south of Highway 237 to prevent flooding in Alviso due to overflow in the immediate upstream area.
Flooding from intrusion of San Francisco Bay waters also presents a serious hazard to the Alviso community. The attached Tide Level Diagram shows diagramatically the different stages of the tide in the Alviso area. What this translates into is that if, at the point of the highest high tide level, which is likely to be reached every 2 years, an additional 3 foot wave action would break the levees and inundate all lands below an elevation of ten (10) feet mean sea level. This breaking could result from over-topping or failure in a seismic event. Concomitant with this threat is fresh water flooding from the mouths of the Guadalupe River and Coyote Creek when filled with storm waters pushed back by wind-driven bay waves and abnormally high tides.
Complete flood protection for Alviso would necessitate an elaborate system of inboard and outboard levees, the exact configuration and detail unknown at present.
